- en_conflict_test_verified: 168

The probe script is already running without crashing, which suggests it's either truncating the ZH activations to match the 966 labels or the results are only valid for the first 966 entries. Let me examine how the script handles this size mismatch.

Wait — the ZH activations from v1 don't correspond to the same samples as the v2 JSONL labels, so even truncation would give mismatched data. This means the Qwen probe results are likely invalid: the ZH→ZH and EN→ZH accuracies are probably bogus because the test data is misaligned, and ZH→EN is compromised because the training data doesn't match. The EN→EN result should be reliable since it only uses English data. I need to check the probe script to confirm how it's handling this mismatch.

each accuracy significantly above chance (50%)?\\n  - Permutation test (1000 iters): is the layer-wise peak accuracy above noise?\\n\\nOutput:\\n  - Console table with per-layer accuracy + p-values\\n  - probe_results.json   (structured results)\\n  - probe_accuracy_by_layer.png  (visualization)\\n\\nDependencies: torch, numpy, sklearn, scipy, matplotlib\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nimport argparse\\nimport json\\nfrom pathlib import Path\\n\\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\\nimport numpy as np\\nimport torch\\nfrom scipy import stats\\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\\nfrom sklearn.metrics import balanced_accuracy_score, f1_score\\nfrom sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler\\n\\n\\nDIRECTIONS = [\\\"EN→EN\\\", \\\"ZH→ZH\\\", \\\"EN→ZH\\\", \\\"ZH→EN\\\"]\\n\\n\\ndef load_activations(path: str) -> dict:\\n    data = torch.load(path, map_location=\\\"cpu\\\", weights_only=True)\\n    n_train = data[\\\"split_sizes\\\"][\\\"train\\\"]\\n    acts = data[\\\"activations\\\"]\\n    if acts.dtype == torch.bfloat16:\\n        acts = acts.float()\\n    return {\\n        \\\"train_X\\\": acts[:n_train],\\n        \\\"train_y\\\": data[\\\"labels\\\"][:n_train],\\n        \\\"test_X\\\": acts[n_train:],\\n        \\\"test_y\\\": data[\\\"labels\\\"][n_train:],\\n    }\\n\\n\\ndef train_and_eval(\\n    train_X: np.ndarray,\\n    train_y: np.ndarray,\\n    test_X: np.ndarray,\\n    test_y: np.ndarray,\\n) -> tuple[float, float, float]:\\n    scaler = StandardScaler()\\n    train_X = scaler.fit_transform(train_X)\\n    test_X = scaler.transform(test_X)\\n    clf = LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced', max_iter=1000, solver=\\\"lbfgs\\\")\\n    clf.fit(train_X, train_y)\\n    y_pred = clf.predict(test_X)\\n    acc = float(np.mean(y_pred == test_y))\\n    bal_acc = balanced_accuracy_score(test_y, y_pred)\\n    f1 = f1_score(test_y, y_pred)\\n    return acc, bal_acc, f1\\n\\n\\ndef binomial_p(accuracy: float, n: int, chance: float = 0.5) -> float:\\n    k = int(round(accuracy * n))\\n    return stats.binomtest(k, n, chance, alternative=\\\"greater\\\").pvalue\\n\\n\\ndef permutation_test(\\n    train_X: np.ndarray,\\n    train_y: np.ndarray,\\n    test_X: np.ndarray,\\n    test_y: np.ndarray,\\n    observed_acc: float,\\n    n_perm: int = 1000,\\n    rng_seed: int = 42,\\n) -> float:\\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(rng_seed)\\n    count = 0\\n    for _ in range(n_perm):\\n        perm_y = rng.permutation(train_y)\\n        acc, _, _ = train_and_eval(train_X, perm_y, test_X, test_y)\\n        if acc >= observed_acc:\\n            count += 1\\n    return count / n_perm\\n\\n\\ndef run_direction(\\n    train_data: dict,\\n    test_data: dict,\\n    num_layers: int,\\n    direction_name: str,\\n    run_permutation: bool = True,\\n) -> list[dict]:\\n    train_y = train_data[\\\"train_y\\\"].numpy()\\n    test_y = test_data[\\\"test_y\\\"].numpy()\\n    n_test = len(test_y)\\n\\n    results = []\\n    best_acc, best_layer = 0.0, 0\\n\\n    for layer in range(num_layers):\\n        train_X = train_data[\\\"train_X\\\"][:, layer, :].numpy()\\n        test_X = test_data[\\\"test_X\\\"][:, layer, :].numpy()\\n\\n        acc, bal_acc, f1 = train_and_eval(train_X, train_y, test_X, test_y)\\n        p_binom = binomial_p(acc, n_test)\\n\\n        results.append({\\n            \\\"layer\\\": layer,\\n            \\\"accuracy\\\": round(acc, 4),\\n            \\\"balanced_accuracy\\\": round(bal_acc, 4),\\n            \\\"f1\\\": round(f1,
